title: Creative assistance: Planned test proves no gains
desc: Outlines an augmentation experiment measuring novelty and usefulness, but unlike outcome studies it supplies only a prespecified research design.

kps.k: The cluster concerns AI-assisted creativity, but the supplied evidence describes a planned test rather than demonstrated gains or homogenisation.
kps.d: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces the Collective Diversity of Novel Content frames a potential tension between individual creativity and collective diversity. However, the supplied excerpts identify an anonymised preregistration with no study data yet collected. They establish a research question about creators’ and third parties’ evaluations of short stories, not the outcomes asserted in the title. The material presents no substantive disagreement between sources.

kps.k: The design tests AI as an aid to human idea generation, not a replacement for the writer.
kps.d: The authors plan to compare unaided writing with access to one or up to five AI-generated story ideas through OpenAI’s ChatGPT API. They propose 300 completing creators, split equally across conditions, and 400 third-party evaluators, each rating six randomly drawn stories. This comparison could inform whether access to AI ideas, and the amount of access, changes evaluations of human-written output; it does not test autonomous content production.

kps.k: The planned measures distinguish perceived novelty and usefulness, but do not establish collective diversity effects.
kps.d: Creators and third-party evaluators would assess novelty and usefulness through separate three-question indices on one-to-five scales. The authors also propose exploratory measures of enjoyment, writing quality, humour and boredom, alongside differences associated with participants’ creativity. These measures broaden the assessment beyond a single creativity score. Nevertheless, the supplied excerpts report no results and do not specify a collective-diversity measure, so they cannot support conclusions about homogenisation or which writers benefit most.

kps.k: Interpretation of any eventual results must account for the prespecified analysis and exclusions.
kps.d: The authors plan regressions and robustness checks, with aggregate indices and component-level analysis. They would pool the AI conditions in the main analysis if their principal outcomes do not differ statistically, while reporting all three conditions separately in an appendix. They would exclude noncompleters and unaided participants who acknowledge AI use. These choices define the intended comparison; practical recommendations about adopting AI for creative work require results rather than the preregistration alone.

vlens.an: The academia-and-research source supports the cluster’s principal proposition. Its supplied excerpts describe a preregistered experiment—not reported empirical findings—so they cannot establish either the individual creativity gains or the reduction in collective diversity suggested by the article’s title. The design also matches the cluster’s augmentation framing: human participants write stories with no AI assistance or with access to one or more AI-generated ideas, rather than delegating story production autonomously. The source further specifies planned evaluation dimensions, analyses and exclusions, but these are methodological commitments rather than outcome evidence. There is no material internal disagreement in the supplied record; the principal qualification is evidentiary, distinguishing what the planned study could test from what the excerpts actually demonstrate. Because this professional-voice category contains only one curated source here, its position should not be generalized to academia or research as a whole.

elens.an: The 2023–2024 source supports the cluster’s principal proposition. Its supplied material is a preregistered experimental design with no collected study data, so it cannot establish either individual creativity gains or reduced collective diversity despite those claims appearing in the source title. It also aligns with the proposition’s augmentation framing: human participants write the stories, while generative AI supplies one or up to five story ideas. The design materially specifies intended comparisons, measures and analyses, but these are plans rather than findings. There is no substantive internal variation in the supplied evidence: the only source consistently distinguishes the proposed test from demonstrated outcomes. Because the corpus is curated and this facet contains one source, this assessment characterises that source only and does not indicate the prevalence of this view during 2023–2024.
